claims.claim_text: The indexed William E. Fairbairn is British close-combat instructor William Ewart “Dan” Fairbairn.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NPS history supplies the expanded middle name, British Army captaincy, Shanghai police career, SOE instruction, April 1942 loan to OSS, and later lieutenant-colonel rank.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the uncommon exact name, British index note, nationality, and direct OSS instructional role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history dates the Shanghai retirement to 1940 and the SOE-to-OSS transfer to April 1942.
claims.match_notes: Box 226 remains unreviewed; the source index itself prints no rank.

claims.claim_text: Fairbairn's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the British Special Operations Executive, which lent him to OSS in April 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history explicitly sequences SOE teaching in Britain and Canada and a loan to OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the same official account identifies the unusual full name and OSS role.
claims.match_notes: SOE is a government assignment, not a private civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The Shanghai Municipal Police was Fairbairn's last identified civilian employer before his SOE and OSS assignments.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS documents a long Shanghai police career, leadership of a special anti-riot squad, retirement at 55, and return to Britain in 1940.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the career appears in the same official full-name biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before wartime SOE service.
claims.match_notes: The historical police force is preserved separately from later SOE and OSS assignments.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant (junior grade) Frank V. Huston is the naval radio instructor Peter Mero recruited into OSS Communications.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS names Frank V. Huston among three new naval officers and radio instructors recruited in Chicago, then describes his Bari communications work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, middle initial, naval-officer status, radio specialty, Chicago recruitment context, and OSS service align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history places recruitment in 1943.
claims.match_notes: The similarly indexed Frank U. Huston has no rank and remains a separate person entity.

claims.claim_text: Frank V. Huston's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Navy as a naval officer and radio instructor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS explicitly says Peter Mero recruited Huston from the Navy after describing him as a new naval officer and radio instructor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the index's lieutenant-junior-grade rank independently matches the official narrative.
claims.match_notes: No civilian employer is substituted for this military pathway.

claims.claim_text: During the 1930s, Huston learned radio operation in the United States Coast Guard.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history identifies the Coast Guard as the source of his radio experience but does not specify dates or duty status.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the statement is part of the same Frank Huston OSS recruitment narrative.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar military or maritime-service affiliation.
claims.match_notes: Box 359 may distinguish regular, reserve, or auxiliary status.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Corporal Edward E. Nicholas Jr. is the Illinois engineering student and Army Signal Corps trainee recruited into OSS Communications.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS supplies the exact full name and suffix, Rock Island origin, engineering field, Signal Corps program, corporal rank, and 1943 OSS training.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, suffix, middle initial, corporal rank, and OSS communications role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences university study, Signal Corps training, and OSS recruitment in 1943.
claims.match_notes: The full index service number remains private.

claims.claim_text: Nicholas's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was an Army Signal Corps advanced microwave program.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS directly sequences the Signal Corps program, University of Chicago training, and OSS recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the same official narrative matches the exact person and corporal rank.
claims.match_notes: The military program is kept distinct from both university affiliations.

claims.claim_text: Nicholas was an electrical-engineering student at the University of Illinois before entering the Signal Corps program.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history identifies his field and university and then sequences the Army program.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the exact-name account belongs to the indexed corporal.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar or wartime student status before OSS.
claims.match_notes: University attendance is not classified as employment.

claims.claim_text: Nicholas studied advanced microwave design at the University of Chicago through the Army Signal Corps program.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The source identifies the university as the training location and the Signal Corps as the sponsoring military organization.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; this is part of the same exact-name chronology.
claims.match_notes: The University of Chicago is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Vincent L. Gonzalez Jr. is the Havana-born merchant mariner and commercial telegrapher recruited into OSS Communications.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS supplies the exact full name and suffix, 1918 Havana birth, New York upbringing, Merchant Marine service, FCC license, and OSS Madrid assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, suffix, middle initial, distinctive biography, Spanish fluency, and OSS communications role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history dates the commercial telegraph license to December 1943 and recruitment soon afterward.
claims.match_notes: The index row has no rank or serial; Box 281 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Gonzalez's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Merchant Marine as a commercial telegrapher.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS sequences joining the Merchant Marine, obtaining an FCC commercial telegraph license in December 1943, and OSS recruitment soon afterward.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the same detailed official account identifies the exact person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate professional affiliation in late 1943.
claims.match_notes: The Merchant Marine is not treated as a single named employer; a shipping company is not guessed.

claims.claim_text: After high school, Gonzalez worked as a runner for an employer not named in the reviewed source.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history documents the occupation before marriage and Merchant Marine service but supplies no employer or dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the occupation appears in the same detailed full-name biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar or pre-OSS work, not established as immediate or the last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: No organization is invented and the role is excluded from the last-civilian-employer field.

claims.claim_text: The indexed T-5 Roger L. Belanger is the French-speaking Army radio operator recruited into OSS Communications.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS supplies the exact name and middle initial, South Portland-area origin, age at enlistment, Army radio training, French fluency, and OSS assignments.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, middle initial, enlisted technician status, radio specialty, and OSS chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history dates Army entry to February 1943 and OSS training to September-November 1943.
claims.match_notes: The full index service number remains private.

claims.claim_text: Belanger's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Army Air Corps radio-operator training.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS explicitly states that OSS recruited him from the Army Air Corps because of his radio skill and French fluency.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the index's T-5 grade independently matches the enlisted Army pathway.
claims.match_notes: No civilian employer is substituted for the documented military pathway.

research_attempts.query_text: "William E Fairbairn" OSS; "William Ewart Fairbairn" employer; Shanghai Municipal Police; SOE; NARA index, NARA web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, institutional, book, obituary, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and Wikidata were discovery-only; firearms and martial-arts sites were derivative; an unrelated nineteenth-century ship record was a namesake; no exact-name CIA result improved on the official NPS chronology.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the identity, explicit SOE-to-OSS transfer, and last civilian Shanghai police employer without collapsing government assignment and employment.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 226 for formal loan, rank, and Shanghai career documentation.

research_attempts.query_text: "Frank V Huston" OSS; Navy radio instructor Chicago; Coast Guard 1930s; NARA index, NARA web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, university yearbook, obituary, directory, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Search noise and an Illinois yearbook name hit did not independently establish OSS identity; the unranked Frank U. Huston index row was retained as a separate person; no exact CIA result was accepted.
research_attempts.research_notes: The matching middle initial, naval rank, radio specialty, and official NPS recruitment narrative support high-confidence identity and an explicit Navy pathway.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 359 for Navy and Coast Guard service chronology and any civilian employer.

research_attempts.research_notes: Verified an Army Signal Corps immediate pathway and preserved both university relationships as student or training affiliations, not employers.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 559 for program dates, Army orders, and any civilian employment.
